subject: Post-demo: Streaming & tool-call onramp + POC success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@ledgerlane.com>
Cc: Adam Cho <adam.cho@ledgerlane.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Streaming & tool-call onramp + POC success criteria

Elena / Adam — great meeting today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC timeline: 

Call recap:
- Use case: conversational ledger reconciliation for high-volume merchant transactions (search + structured extraction + tool call to accounting system).
- Key constraints: p95 latency target, sample volume ~150k calls/day during trial, SSO + audit log requirement.

Proposed POC success criteria (please confirm):
1) Accuracy: >= 90% mapping rate for reconciliation intents across a 2k-batch test set.
2) Latency: end-to-end p95 < 500ms for streaming generate + tool call.
3) Stability: no more than 1% retry rate over 48 hour stress run.
4) Integration: SDK-based streaming implementation with tool-calls to your accounting API working end-to-end.

Suggested timeline:
- Tech kickoff (1 week): environment access, test data, SSO & network checks.
- Integration sprint (2 weeks): SDK integration, API routes, tool-call wiring, basic instrumentation.
- Eval run (1 week): run acceptance tests, collect metrics, iterate.

Owners:
- Redwood: Ben Carter (sales) — POC owner / cadence; Soojin Lee (solutions engineer) — technical lead; Marissa Cole (cs) — success criteria & acceptance.
- LedgerLane: Elena Morales — product owner; Adam Cho — engineering contact.

Attachments: I’ve included a compact POC checklist and a sample metrics CSV to seed acceptance tests. I’ll follow up with an integration snippet for your engineers.

Next steps: if the criteria and timeline look good, can you confirm Adam as the primary tech contact and share a short list of sample test records (anonymized) by EOD Thursday?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (12 KB)

From: Elena Morales <elena@ledgerlane.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Cho <adam.cho@ledgerlane.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Streaming & tool-call onramp + POC success criteria

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we’re aligned on the high level. A few clarifications and constraints from our side: 

Clarifications:
- Accuracy target: our internal bar is closer to 92% for reconciliation intent; 90% minimum is fine for the POC as long as we show a path to 92% with prompt/test iterations.
- Latency: 500ms p95 is ambitious but acceptable if you can demonstrate streaming + tool-call latency within that window.

Constraints:
- Data residency: trial data must stay in our us-west region and logs retained for 90 days.
- Auth: SAML SSO and service-account-based API keys for tooling; we’ll provide details during kickoff.

Tech contacts: Adam will lead integration (adam.cho@ledgerlane.com). I’ll be the product sponsor (elena@ledgerlane.com).

We’ll share a scrubbed dataset (2k records) by Friday morning. Go ahead and schedule the tech kickoff — Adam and I are available Friday 10–12 PT or Monday 9–11 PT.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Product, LedgerLane
elena@ledgerlane.com

Great — Friday 10am PT works for the Redwood tech kickoff. I’ve penciled it in and invited Soojin to lead the session. 

High-level integration plan (what we’ll cover in kickoff):
- Network & auth: SAML SSO, IP allowlist, service-account keys, and log-forwarding endpoint.
- SDK path: we recommend using Redwood’s Node SDK for streaming generate; it will simplify tool-calling and reconnect logic. We'll provide a minimal snippet.
- API routes: primary endpoints you’ll call during POC: /v1/stream/generate (websocket/stream), /v1/call/tool (synchronous tool invocation fallback), /v1/kv/cache (optional prefix caching).
- Tool-calling pattern: streaming generate emits tool-call frames when the model requests an external lookup; Redwood provides a small helper to surface tool-call events to your code, handle auth, and resume streaming once the tool responds.
- Observability: Telemetry hooks for per-request latency, token counts, and retry classification. We’ll ship a sample Grafana dashboard.

Acceptance tests we will run during Eval run:
- 2k sample run for intent mapping accuracy.
- 24h stability run at target sample rate to measure retries and token usage.

Internal owners (confirmed):
- Soojin Lee — technical kickoff + SDK walkthrough.
- Marissa Cole — acceptance test definitions and gating.
- Jordan Blake — platform contact for networking and VPC questions.

I’m attaching a short integration snippet and the POC checklist. See you Friday.

Ben

Attachment: integration-snippet.md (4 KB); poc-eval-metrics.csv (2 KB)

Adam / team — quick tech notes ahead of Friday’s kickoff so your engineers can look over before the call: 

1) Minimal Node SDK example (streaming + tool call):
- Connect to wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate with service-account token.
- On tool-call frame: SDK emits event {toolRequest}, you perform external HTTP POST to your accounting API /reconcile, return result to SDK helper, call helper.resume(result).
- SDK will handle KV cache lookups automatically if you configure prefix caching and provide a small key resolver function.

2) Network & Auth checklist:
- Provide us the SAML metadata URL for SSO test account.
- IP allowlist: add Redwood egress range x.x.x.32/27 (we'll confirm exact CIDR before kickoff).

3) Acceptance test wiring:
- We’ll add an instrumentation flag in the SDK run to emit per-request telemetry to your dedicated metrics endpoint. Please confirm an endpoint or we will default to pushing to the Redwood dashboard for the POC.

4) Logs & retention: we’ll retain request logs for 90 days in your region and supply an audit export for compliance review.

I’ve pasted a very short snippet in the attached integration-snippet.md and added comments about the tool-call flow. If Adam’s team can send a small sample of token-limited credentials for a staging accounting endpoint, we’ll wire that in on Friday and demo an end-to-end flow.

See the attached POC checklist and metrics CSV for the evaluation gates.

— Soojin

- We prefer the SDK approach (Node) for the streaming path.
